sources.title: Udo Seifert, Stochastic thermodynamics: From principles to the cost of precision (complete lecture notes, 2017)

contents.name: Finite-state transition rates and master equation

source_review.read_extent: Read §2.2, covering constant transition rates and the finite-state master equation.
source_review.supports: The finite-state Markov jump-process convention and forward rate equation.
source_review.limitations: The item fixes its own bounded continuous time-dependent rate convention and makes no claim that a physical system realizes it.

contents.name: Trajectory weights, holding factors and reversal

source_review.read_extent: Read §4.1, the complete ordered-jump-time path-weight formula and its no-jump boundary case.
source_review.supports: The product of jump rates and survival factors used in the local path-density proof.
source_review.limitations: The lecture notes present the formula; the local lemma also proves the bounded-rate tail estimate and finite expected jump count.

source_review.read_extent: Read §2.2 on the master equation for a discrete state space.
source_review.supports: The incoming-minus-outgoing flow convention for the row generator.
source_review.limitations: The item supplies a complete local derivation for bounded continuous rates and proves the invariant-law consequence.

source_review.read_extent: Read §§4.1–4.3, including the path likelihood ratio, time reversal and the stochastic entropy boundary term.
source_review.supports: The dimensionless log ratio of forward and reversed stationary path weights.
source_review.limitations: The local definition makes the finite-state rates, positive stationary law and symmetric-support conditions explicit and does not identify the statistic with physical reservoir entropy without additional assumptions.

source_review.read_extent: Read §5.2, which gives the forward/backward jump-count means for the asymmetric walk, and §4.1 for finite-state path weights.
source_review.supports: The rate-times-occupation interpretation of expected directed jump counts.
source_review.limitations: The lecture notes use the intensity formula in their model; the item proves the finite-horizon identity from the displayed path densities.

source_review.read_extent: Read §3.2.1 and §4.4, where the Jarzynski identity is recovered from the Crooks relation for stochastic dynamics.
source_review.supports: The exponential-work identity and its path-reversal context.
source_review.limitations: The lecture notes do not state the finite-state weighted endpoint ODE; the local lemma proves that equation and uniqueness under bounded continuous rates.

source_review.read_extent: Read §§4.1–4.3, including the forward/reverse path ratio and the finite-time measure relation.
source_review.supports: Cancellation of holding-time factors, reversal of the jump sequence, and the finite-time fluctuation identity.
source_review.limitations: The local proof states and verifies the exact finite-state measure identity without requiring a density for the entropy variable.

source_review.read_extent: Read §§2.4 and 4.4, including time-dependent driving, reversed protocols and the work/free-energy relation.
source_review.supports: The endpoint partition-function identity under the stated thermal and rate assumptions.
source_review.limitations: The local item proves its finite-state version directly by the finite-dimensional weighted forward equation and states instantaneous detailed balance as an input.
